reviewedRevision: 5ef589b plus the rework in this commit
process: Lean final review at the user's request: the known 3-level shortfall went straight to a retrofit, followed by one independent review round, one clean-worktree test run and a short browser check.
independentProbes: The reviewer's own reaction-limited bot, reading only public state, cleared 120 of 120 runs at 0.25 s and 119 of 120 at 0.35 s (20 levels, 6 seeds, 60 Hz), most levels in 3-25 s. Ninety blind patterns (idle, mash, random keys and 72 hold-plus-alternate timings) won at most 1.7% of any level from 3. An exhaustive search with the game's own rotation and clearing rules found every fixed-supply level solvable: levels 6, 11, 14 and 17 need 3, 4, 7 and 9 of their 8, 11, 13 and 15 pieces. Burst levels never depend on luck because the 7-bag always deals an I piece and hold is available. Fuzz with hostile dt and pointer values, determinism at 30, 60 and 120 Hz, broken progress stores and EN/ZH text fit all passed.

findings.observation: Only 3 districts in a partial table, with no select or continue. There are now 20 data-driven districts with four goal kinds (clear lines, burst several rows with one piece, dig out marked rubble, finish with a fixed piece supply), gravity from 0.80 to 0.30 s per row, accurate EN/ZH tips, a district select and env.progress continue.

Every district opens with a 2.4 s reading pause with gravity and input frozen and no overlay over the well; the 875-line file is split into seven modules with a quality test file covering per-level clears, blind bars, a reaction-limited bot, determinism, hostile input, broken stores and terminal state.

openNotes: A piece resting flush against a wall cannot rotate toward that wall (16 cases); rotating the other way works and lock delay leaves time to nudge away.
On district 3 one misplaced piece can clear a preset row and shorten the shaft, so the 4-row burst needs a rebuild; X retries the district.
Rubble districts 13 and 16 are slow for a heuristic bot; human play is unmeasured.

browser.method: Official Claude in Chrome extension, local server; real clicks on Start, Play again, the language switch and the touch buttons, synthetic in-page keys; only DOM text and the canvas were read.
observed: Chinese: Start opened district 1 of 20 (基础区, clear 4 lines) with the tip in the right panel and the well uncovered; Space hard-dropped pieces and the score rose.
Chinese loss: stacking to the top ended the run with the explanation 第1区：方块已堆到井顶。; Play again restarted district 1.
English 390 px phone frame (388 px inner, no horizontal overflow): eight touch buttons; Left moved the piece, Turn rotated it and Drop placed it (score 34).
Not covered in the browser: a district win and the district select, which appears only after a first clear; the reviewer's bots and the quality tests cover both.
